transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I'm here because I've been having a... a real problem with eating lately. What scares me most is that once I start eating, I just can't seem to stop. It feels like my hands just keep reaching for more food, even while I’m sitting there telling myself, Tom, stop this right now. But I just can't. So, that's what brought me in.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories you consumed?

Yes, I do. Well, there are times after I eat too much... I'll go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. And I’ve also taken laxatives. I just get so scared that all that food is going to stay in me after I lose control like that. So, yes, I do try to get rid of it.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirmed behaviors of self-induced vomiting and laxative use after eating, which aligns with bulimia nervosa (F50.2). This rules out anorexia nervosa (F50.0) due to absence of restrictive eating as a primary behavior, and eliminates unspecified feeding or eating disorder (F50.9).
